body.statement:
Uniformly over fixed \(S\) and all positive sample sizes, let
\[
 C_{\lambda,d}:=\frac{2\lambda}{2\lambda+d}
 +\frac{d}{2\lambda+d}(\log2)^{-2\lambda/d}.
\]
Then
\[
 R_{\mathrm{sm}}
 \leq C_{\lambda,d}
 \bigl(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\bigr),
 \qquad
 R_{\star,\beta}
 \asymp_{\lambda,d}
 R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
Consequently, in any experiment for which \(R_{\star,\beta}\) is established
as the sharp risk, the oracle region is
\[
 N^{-\kappa}=o\bigl(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\bigr),
\]
the generated-center region is
\[
 R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}=o(N^{-\kappa}),
\]
and the boundary is
\[
 N\asymp
 \bigl(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\bigr)^{-1/\kappa}.
\]
Under a stricter independent-design or fixed-query condition that delivers the
comparator spacing term \(R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-2\lambda/d}\), one instead has
the exact relations
\[
 R_{\mathrm{sm}}\leq R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}},
 \qquad
 R_\star=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:exact-training-coordinates} removes a classical
measurement-error inverse problem from the historical design; accordingly the
defined bookkeeping contains neither a deconvolution term nor a separate
moving-Gram rate.  Finally, \(R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-1}\) whenever
\(\lambda>1\).  These algebraic conclusions do not by themselves assert that
either frontier is sharp for a statistical experiment.
body.justification: The exact diagram distinguishes a genuinely active information channel from a bookkeeping term and records higher-order saturation.
body.gap: The repeated-measurement literature has a sparse-to-dense smoothing transition, while generated-regressor and measurement-error papers imply different first-stage effects; no existing result locates this oracle boundary.
body.consumer: A study can allocate its data budget to the active axis and avoid unnecessary deconvolution when the historical paths are exact.
body.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 a:=\frac{2\lambda}{2\lambda+d}\in(0,1),
 \qquad
 q:=\frac{2\lambda}{d}>0.
\]
We first derive the scalar inequality used below.  For \(u>0\), let
\(\phi(u):=au+(1-a)-u^a\).  Then \(\phi(1)=0\) and
\[
 \phi'(u)=a(1-u^{a-1}).
\]
Because \(a-1<0\), the derivative is negative on \((0,1)\) and positive on
\((1,\infty)\).  Hence \(\phi(u)\geq 0\) for every \(u>0\).  Substitution of
\(u=x/y\), followed by multiplication by \(y>0\), gives
\[
 x^a y^{1-a}\leq ax+(1-a)y,
 \qquad x,y>0.
\]
The definitions of \(a\) and \(q\) give \(q(1-a)=a\).  Therefore, for each
cohort \(s\), positivity of \(T\) and \(n_s\) permits the preceding inequality
with \(x=n_s^{-1}\) and \(y=T^{-q}\), yielding
\[
 (Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
 =(n_s^{-1})^a(T^{-q})^{1-a}
 \leq a n_s^{-1}+(1-a)T^{-q}.
\]
Since \(T\geq1\), one has \(\log(T\vee2)\geq\log2>0\).  Thus the corrected
spacing definition in \texttt{def:rate-frontier} implies
\[
 T^{-q}
 \leq (\log2)^{-q}
 \left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}{T}\right\}^{q}
 =(\log2)^{-q}R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}.
\]
Multiplying the cohortwise bound by \(\pi_s^2\), summing over \(s\), and using
\(\sum_s\pi_s^2\leq(\sum_s\pi_s)^2=1\), which follows from positivity and
\(\sum_s\pi_s=1\), gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 R_{\mathrm{sm}}
 &\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}
   +(1-a)T^{-q}\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s^2\\
 &\leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}
   +(1-a)(\log2)^{-q}R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\\
 &\leq C_{\lambda,d}
   \bigl(R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\bigr),
 \end{aligned}
\]
where
\[
 C_{\lambda,d}:=a+(1-a)(\log2)^{-q}\geq1.
\]
Let
\[
 A:=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta},
 \qquad
 D:=A\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]
The corrected frontier definition and the last display imply, equation by
equation,
\[
 D\leq R_{\star,\beta}
 =A\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sm}}
 \leq C_{\lambda,d}D.
\]
This proves
\(R_{\star,\beta}\asymp_{\lambda,d}
R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}\), uniformly
in the positive sample sizes; the constants do not depend on \(N\), \(T\), or
\(\mathbf n\).

By \texttt{def:rate-frontier}, \(R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-\kappa}\), whereas
\(A\) is independent of \(N\).  Consequently the donor contribution is
asymptotically negligible exactly in the oracle region
\[
 N^{-\kappa}=o(A),
\]
and it dominates exactly in the generated-center region
\[
 A=o(N^{-\kappa}).
\]
Equality up to positive constants, \(N^{-\kappa}\asymp A\), is equivalent,
because \(\kappa>0\), to
\[
 N\asymp A^{-1/\kappa}.
\]
These comparisons become minimax phases whenever a separate sharp-risk theorem
establishes \(R_{\star,\beta}\) for the experiment in question.

For the stricter independent-design or fixed-query comparator, retain
\(R_{\mathrm{sp}}=T^{-q}\).  The same cohortwise inequality, without the
logarithmic comparison, gives
\[
 R_{\mathrm{sm}}
 \leq aR_{\mathrm{tr}}+(1-a)R_{\mathrm{sp}}
 \leq R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}.
\]
The comparator definition of \(R_\star\) therefore yields the exact identity
\[
 R_\star=R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp}}\vee R_{\mathrm{don}}.
\]

Assumption \texttt{ass:exact-training-coordinates} states
\(X_{st}^{\mathrm{obs}}=X_{st}\).  Hence using the recorded historical
coordinate does not require inversion of a measurement-error convolution.
Inspection of \texttt{def:rate-frontier} then confirms that its bookkeeping has
no deconvolution component and no separately postulated moving-Gram rate.  This
is an algebraic and observation-structure conclusion, not an independent
sharpness claim.  Finally, \(\kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\}\); thus \(\lambda>1\)
implies \(\kappa=1\), and the donor term is
\(R_{\mathrm{don}}=N^{-1}\), proving higher-smoothness saturation.
